title: centralize-eval-ci-trigger-and-lightweight-load-smoke-refactor
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Consolidate CI triggers and refactor the evaluation/benchmarking harness to provide a fast smoke path for PRs, maintainable long-running load jobs, and a reproducible eval pipeline. Background: Our current eval pipeline is fragmented: multiple Jenkins/cron jobs, ad-hoc GitHub Actions workflows, and a separate scheduled GKE job that runs full-load scenarios. This fragmentation increases maintenance overhead, causes flaky signal in perf regressions, and lengthens developer feedback loops. Goals: - Single CI entry-point for evaluation runs (PR smoke, nightly regression, weekly full-load) implemented in GitHub Actions with a lightweight dispatcher. - Introduce a fast smoke harness (<6m) that runs sampled representative scenarios and synthetic traces for immediate feedback on PRs. - Clean up long-run load harness into a reproducible GKE Job with versioned artifacts, better checkpointing, and deterministic seeds. - Upgrade test harness dependencies (pytest->8.3, locust->2.12, protobuf->4.x) and add a compatibility shim for older runner configs. - Standardize metrics export (Prometheus metrics + structured JSON artifacts uploaded to S3) and add an aggregator script that produces the perf-regression-delta artifact consumed by console/regression alerting. Scope and non-goals: - This ticket focuses on CI orchestration, harness refactor, and artifact packaging. It does NOT change model-serving code, nor introduce new load generators for different model architectures. Acceptance criteria: 1) PRs get a <6 minute smoke evaluation that verifies core paths (inference latency, KV-cache behavior, end-to-end correctness) and blocks on obvious regressions. 2) Nightly regression produces stable artifacts with reproducible metrics, uploaded to s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/{runtime}/{date}/ and a summary JSON that the Console can ingest. 3) Full-load GKE job can be triggered from the new dispatcher and supports resume from last checkpoint. 4) All test dependencies upgraded, and a compatibility shim is documented for legacy workflows. 5) Documentation: Confluence runbook, GitHub Actions matrix docs, and one internal demo session recorded. Migration plan: - Phase 1 (week 1): Prototype GH Actions dispatcher + smoke harness in repo eval/ci-scripts. - Phase 2 (week 2-3): Convert scheduled jobs to dispatcher triggers; implement S3 artifact uploader and metrics exporter. - Phase 3 (week 4): Migrate full-load job to GKE Job with checkpointing; run side-by-side for two nights. - Phase 4 (week 5): Flip defaults, decommission old Jenkins cron, add alerts and a rollback plan. Risk & trade-offs: - Short smoke suite may miss low-frequency regressions; mitigate by careful scenario sampling and keeping long-run regression intact. - Upgrading locust/protobuf may surface flaky integrations; will gate upgrades behind CI matrix and compatibility shim. Notes & links: - Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Eval+Harness+Modernization - Prototype GH Actions: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/472 - Draft runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Eval+Runbook - S3 artifact path convention: s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/{runtime}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/{job-type}/{run-id}/
comments: 2026-02-12 Maya Chen: Created ticket after spike with EngOps and Platform. Identified three source schedulers (legacy-jenkins, legacy-cron, eval-gke) and multiple ad-hoc scripts.

2026-02-16 Liam O'Neill: Implemented GH Actions dispatcher prototype (see PR #472). Smoke harness runs basic latency and correctness checks in ~3m on an m6i runner. Observed flakiness in protobuf serialization on locust 2.x — added a repro test.
2026-02-20 Maya Chen: Decision to upgrade to locust 2.12 and protobuf 4.x; added compatibility shim layer to handle older binary fixtures temporarily. PM reviewed and agreed on rollout plan.

2026-02-25 EngOps (review): Suggested S3 artifact retention policy of 90 days and to push metrics to Prometheus via pushgateway for short-lived jobs. Also recommended using a dedicated service account for GKE jobs.

2026-03-03 Liam O'Neill: Completed migration of nightly scheduler to dispatcher and wired artifact uploader. Nightly run 2026-03-03 succeeded and generated reproducible artifacts. Planning full-load side-by-side tests next week (GKE job).
